column1: # Interface-review decisions Q1-Q15 (maintainer, 2026-11-17) and their status.

column3: (a) Retire the early rootfs world (erfs*, early_*, product_*, ramtab, bpath/bpivot) once the common VFS/process path boots both ISAs from the block image.
column4: ARM64 mounts its vda root through vfs_init_root() (root=/dev/vda) like x86 mounts hda; erfs*/early_*/product_* sources, fs/{ramtab,bpath,bpivot,bpivot_boot}.c, their headers and the syscall_context_provider layer are deleted; architecture_guard.py [retired-file] and retired_api_names.txt reject them (early_clock.h, the live pre-timer clock hook, stays).

column3: (a) Each syscall implementation lives in its owner (fs/, mm/, net/, kernel/signals/, ...); only entry and dispatch stay in kernel/entry/.
column4: kernel/entry/ holds syscall_dispatch.c and syscall_table.c; futex, signal and kexec syscalls live with their owners; fs_*, io, mm_*, process, socket, epoll, swap and time syscalls remain in kernel/syscalls/.

column3: (a) Pseudo filesystems become full vfs_fstype mounts with inode and file operations; the named_* side tables become inodes of the parent filesystem.
(a) Platform device drivers live in drivers/<class>/ for both ISAs; arch/ keeps only CPU, MMU and entry code.
column4: GICv2, BCM2836, PL011, serial, RTC and virtio-blk drivers are in drivers/{irq,tty,rtc,virtio}/; arch/x86-64/sources/interrupt/{pic,keyboard}.c remain under arch/.

column3: (b) Arch facades take Linux topic names (asm/io.h, asm/pgtable.h, asm/tlbflush.h, asm/processor.h); includes/ir0/ keeps only portable APIs.
column4: No arch_*.h remains under includes/ or arch/ (names guarded by scripts/retired_api_names.txt); ISA hooks live in arch/{x86-64,arm64}/include/asm/.

column3: (b) Exec and ELF loading move to fs/exec.c and fs/binfmt_elf.c (Linux); the kernel never knows which userspace program runs.
column4: fs/exec.c holds execve and fs/binfmt_elf.c the ELF loader; kernel/exec/{early_elf_stack,saved_environ,vdso}.c remain outside fs/.

column3: (a) The logger moves to kernel/printk/ and the logging.h aliases (lane L1) are retired.
column4: klog is kernel/printk/klog.c with a console registry in kernel/printk/console.c; includes/ir0/logging.h is gone (4bd61262).

column3: Three console layers: tty, console, video driver.
column4: Steps 1-5 and 7 of console-layers.md are done (VT in drivers/tty/vt/vt.c, mirror in drivers/tty/tty_mirror.c, printk console registry); step 6 (one ONLCR policy for fd 1/2 and tty writes) is not done.

column3: (a) mm_struct and the VMAs are owned by mm/.
column4: mm_struct, brk, the VMA list, mmap/munmap/mprotect and free-VA search (mm/va_search.c) are in mm/; kernel/syscalls/{mm_syscalls,mm_brk,mm_vma}.c remain as thin entries.

column3: Rename includes/ir0/wait.h (wait-status macros) to wait_status.h, freeing wait.h for wait queues (X-7).
column4: includes/ir0/wait.h is now includes/ir0/wait_status.h; no source includes ir0/wait.h remain.

column3: Target kernel/{entry,signal,process,time,irq,panic,printk} plus lib/; kernel/main.c stays and is the only loose file in kernel/.
column4: kernel/{entry,signals,process,time,irq,panic,printk} exist; kernel/{boot,exec,futex,kexec,power,sys,syscalls,test} are outside the target list.

column3: (b) Block devices are handles with one name lookup; every device class plugs into one class API with ops and feature flags, as the NIC class does.
column4: Block devices resolve through ir0_block_lookup_by_name to a dev_t handle with struct ir0_block_ops (block/blockdev.c); other device classes do not follow the NIC class pattern yet.

column3: (b) Drivers register through an explicit registration table that is part of the common driver contract.
column4: struct driver_boot_table/driver_boot_entry in includes/ir0/driver_bootstrap.h; tables in drivers/init_drv.c, arch/x86-64/sources/boot_drivers.c and arch/arm64/sources/boot_arch.c run through driver_bootstrap_run().

column3: Delete the IR0-only syscalls (console_scroll, console_clear, keymap_set, keymap_get) in favour of Linux ioctls and escape sequences.
column4: console_scroll and console_clear are gone from includes/ir0/syscall_id.h; keymap_set/get (IR0_SYSCALL_EXTENSION_KEYMAP_*) remain in kernel/entry/syscall_dispatch.c and arch/x86-64/sources/syscall_decode.c.

column3: No weak symbols: required arch hooks fail at link time through a port-contract header; optional generic implementations are chosen explicitly by the build registry; new ISAs start from arch/template/.
column4: No weak symbols remain in kernel sources (architecture_guard.py check 35 enforces it); arch/template/port.h lists the port hooks.
